I am Dr. Agent. Given your fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph node, I need to ask: have you noticed any painless lump in your neck or armpit, or any skin changes?

text: RESULTS: WBC: Elevated, Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased, Platelets: Normal, Lactate_Dehydrogenase: Elevated

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information; while Tuberculosis is a consideration given your history, the specific location of your enlarged nodes and worsening abdominal pain require further investigation. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray and REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_CT_with_contrast. Have you experienced any difficulty swallowing or breathing?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT_Scan_Thorax_and_Abdomen: Findings: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma

The combination of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, and a "massively enlarged" mediastinal mass is highly suggestive of Hodgkin Lymphoma. While Tuberculosis can cause lymphadenopathy, the pattern of massive nodal involvement without mention of pulmonary infiltrates or cavitation on the CT makes it less likely. I need to confirm this with a tissue biopsy and specific markers.

REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide the full resolution CT images for better assessment of the mediastinal mass characteristics.
REQUEST TEST: Excisional_Lymph_Node_Biopsy (Axillary or Cervical)
